answers.brief_reasoning: Differentiate implicitly: 2x + 2y + 2x y' + 4y y' = 0. Solve for y': y' = -(2x+2y)/(2x+4y).
(3,-3) is on the curve because 9 - 18 + 18 = 9. At this point the numerator 2(3) + 2(-3) = 0 and the denominator 2(3) + 4(-3) = -6, so the slope is 0.
The tangent is horizontal when x + y = 0, so y = -x, provided x + 2y ≠ 0. Substituting gives x^2 - 2x^2 + 2x^2 = x^2 = 9, so x = ±3. At both points x + 2y = y ≠ 0.
Differentiate y' = -(x+y)/(x+2y) to get y'' = -[(1+y')(x+2y) - (x+y)(1+2y')]/(x+2y)^2. At (3,-3), y' = 0 and x + y = 0, so y'' = -1/(x+2y) = -1/(-3) = 1/3. Since y'' > 0, the curve is concave up.
answers.final_answer: d²y/dx² = 1/3 > 0, so the curve is concave up at (3,-3)

answers.brief_reasoning: Differentiate implicitly: 2x + y + x y' + 2y y' = 0, so y'(x+2y) = -(2x+y), which gives y' = -(2x+y)/(x+2y).
Check the point: 1 - 2 + 4 = 3, so (-1,2) is on the curve. Slope = -(-2+2)/(-1+4) = 0.
Set 2x + y = 0, so y = -2x. Substitute: x^2 - 2x^2 + 4x^2 = 3x^2 = 3, so x = ±1. At these points x + 2y = -3x ≠ 0, so the slope is defined.
Differentiate again: 2 + 2y' + x y'' + 2(y')^2 + 2y y'' = 0. At (-1,2), y' = 0, so 2 + 3y'' = 0 and y'' = -2/3 < 0.
answers.final_answer: d2y/dx2 = -2/3 < 0, so the curve is concave down at (-1,2)
